evidence.excerpt:
Persistent memory lets language-model agents improve prompts and skills without
updating model weights. We show that matching retrieval scope to certification
scope enables these edits to support reliable repeated adaptation across recurring
task families. We study frozen-model agents on PROCSTREAM-RSI, a 12-round
code-repair stream, using Orthogonal Regression Control (ORC), an execution-
grounded gate for persistent skill edits. In an intervention that holds proposals
and gate decisions fixed, retrieving each accepted skill only for its originating
family raises mean hidden trajectory utility from 0.713 under global memory to
0.816 and changes harmful deployments from six of eight to none. In 27 paired
randomized-order streams, Scoped-ORC improves mean trajectory utility by 0.063
[0.037, 0.094] over Global-ORC, accepts 63 rather than 12 updates, and produces
multiple accepted updates

tor/editor prompt, and at least six answer-free metamorphic checks. For task i and channel

substantial prior competence.
Each round has four discovery and four probe tasks. Separately generated fixed banks contain one
checkpoint and two final tasks per family, for 123 tasks per stream. Exact-output public, private,
and hidden inputs are pairwise disjoint, and hidden cases are unavailable to the online agent. Role-
normalized public views are unique; full manifest-integrity checks are described in the reproducibility
statement and supplement.

checkpoint bank and evaluated once by the terminal state.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured on sealed hidden checkpoint banks and external transfer banks that were never exposed to the online gate or editor.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Hidden trajectory and checkpoint utility on sealed held-out banks, plus external HumanEval+ and GPT-OSS transfer diagnostics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: ORC gate decisions using public, private execution, and metamorphic probe evidence on current and historical family instances.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that unscoped persistent updates induce cross-family regression whereas scoped retrieval eliminates harmful acceptances and increases trajectory utility are directly supported by paired experimental data across multiple seeds and task orders.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations isolate mechanism effects via fixed-output interventions and paired randomized-order extensions (18 and 27 streams), with appropriate matched-compute baselines (Static, Frozen-compute, Latest-only, Replay, Batch-ORC), rigorous bootstrap intervals, and paired sign-flip sensitivity tests.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcomes are measured using sealed hidden checkpoint instances and external benchmarks that were never exposed to the agent or gate selection logic.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Hidden trajectory and checkpoint utility measured on strictly sealed, held-out checkpoint test banks evaluated by an auditor, as well as external HumanEval+ and GPT-OSS transfer banks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Online gating decisions via ORC using public examples, private execution tests, and metamorphic relations on current and historical family probe instances.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly bound their conclusions to inspectable prompt scaffolds under fixed task contracts, noting the lack of open-world routing, wrong-slot misrouting tests, and other model families as areas for future investigation.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, employing a frozen LLM (Qwen3-Coder-Next) on a 12-round procedural stream (PROCSTREAM-RSI) with orthogonal regression control (ORC) that gates skill updates via public, private execution, and metamorphic checks across distinct family slots.
primary.quality_rationale: The study exhibits high experimental rigor with strict leakage boundaries between online probe gates and sealed hidden checkpoints, clear ablation of confounding compute, and robust statistical reporting.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper investigates persistent prompt/skill memory in LLM code-repair agents, diagnosing cross-family interference when locally certified edits are deployed globally and demonstrating that family-scoped retrieval matches deployment scope to certification scope to enable continual adaptation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study exhibits high experimental rigor with strict leakage boundaries between online probe gates and sealed hidden checkpoints, clear ablation of confounding compute, and robust statistical reporting.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly bound their conclusions to inspectable prompt scaffolds under fixed task contracts, noting the lack of open-world routing, wrong-slot misrouting tests, and other model families as areas for future investigation.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
